section: Tribal movements in colonial India - Santhal, Munda (Birsa), Bhil, Rampa, Gond risings
subsections: Tribal revolt → leader + region + present state

Bhil reform movements in Rajasthan and Gujarat

accepted.s:
Match List-I with List-II:

List-I (Revolt)
a. Santhal Hul
b. Munda Ulgulan
c. Kol/Larka rising
d. Khond rising

List-II (Leader)
i. Chakra Bisoi
ii. Birsa Munda
iii. Budhu Bhagat
iv. Sidhu and Kanhu Murmu

Select the correct answer using the code given below.
accepted.x: Santhal Hul was led by Sidhu and Kanhu Murmu, Munda Ulgulan by Birsa Munda, the Kol rising by Budhu Bhagat and the Khond rising by Chakra Bisoi.
accepted.tq: Start from the sure leader–revolt pairs and eliminate the codes.
accepted.sec: Tribal revolt → leader + region + present state  [APPSC]

accepted.s: Which one of the following pairs is correctly matched?
accepted.x: The Bhil rising occurred in Khandesh, in present-day Maharashtra. Bhumij was associated with Manbhum, Tamar with Tamar in Jharkhand and Paika with Khurda in Odisha.
accepted.tq: Use the region column to distinguish closely related tribal revolts.
accepted.sec: Tribal revolt → leader + region + present state  [APPSC]

accepted.s:
Consider the following pairs:
1. Bhumij rising — Ganga Narayan
2. Paika Rebellion — Bakshi Jagabandhu
3. Ramosi uprising — Chittur Singh, Umaji Naik and Bapu Trimbakji Sawant
Which of the pairs given above are correctly matched?
accepted.x: All three pairs are correctly matched. Ganga Narayan led the Bhumij rising, Bakshi Jagabandhu led the Paika Rebellion and the listed leaders were associated with the Ramosi uprisings.
accepted.tq: Check each leader against the corresponding revolt before selecting the coded combination.
accepted.sec: Tribal revolt → leader + region + present state  [APPSC]

accepted.s: The Tamar tribal rising is associated with which one of the following combinations?
o: Oraon tribes and Tamar in Jharkhand
Bhil tribes and Khandesh in Maharashtra
accepted.x: The Tamar rising was associated with the Oraon tribes and the Tamar region of present-day Jharkhand. Its recorded period was 1789–1832.
accepted.tq: Test the tribe–region association rather than relying only on the revolt name.
accepted.sec: Tribal revolt → leader + region + present state  [APPSC]

accepted.s: The British invited the Santhals to settle and cultivate the Rajmahal Hills primarily after they had failed to control the:
accepted.x: The British were unable to control the Paharias of the Rajmahal Hills and therefore invited the Santhals to settle and cultivate the area.
accepted.tq: Identify the immediate colonial administrative response to resistance in the Rajmahal Hills.
accepted.sec: Santhal Hul - Paharias, Rajmahal Hills, outcome  [APPSC]

accepted.s: The tract in the Rajmahal Hills demarcated for Santhal settlement was known as:
accepted.x: The tract demarcated for Santhal settlement and cultivation was called Damin-i-Koh. Kolhan was associated with the administration of the Kol region.
accepted.tq: Use exact administrative terminology to distinguish neighbouring tribal regions.
accepted.sec: Santhal Hul - Paharias, Rajmahal Hills, outcome  [APPSC]

accepted.s: The Santhal Hul began at Bhognadih on:
accepted.x: The Santhal Hul began at Bhognadih on 30 June 1855, observed as Hul Divas.
accepted.tq: Treat the place and exact date as a paired chronology clue.
accepted.sec: Santhal Hul - Paharias, Rajmahal Hills, outcome  [APPSC]

accepted.s:
Consider the following statements regarding the Santhal Hul:
1. About 30,000 Santhals proclaimed Santhal Raj.
2. The revolt was crushed in 1856.
3. More than 15,000 Santhals were killed.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
accepted.x: All three statements are correct. The movement involved about 30,000 Santhals, was crushed in 1856 and caused more than 15,000 deaths.
accepted.tq: Verify the numerical and outcome statements together before choosing the coded option.
accepted.sec: Santhal Hul - Paharias, Rajmahal Hills, outcome  [APPSC]

accepted.s: Which of the following groups was associated with the leadership of the Santhal Hul in addition to Sidhu and Kanhu Murmu?
o: Chand, Bhairav and the sisters Phulo-Jhano
Jatra Bhagat, Govind Giri and Motilal Tejawat
Umaji Naik, Chittur Singh and Narayan Rao
Ganga Narayan, Budhu Bhagat and Tirot Sing
accepted.x: Chand and Bhairav, along with the sisters Phulo and Jhano, were associated with the leadership of the Santhal Hul.
accepted.tq: Distinguish members of one revolt’s leadership from leaders of other tribal movements.
accepted.sec: Santhal Hul - Paharias, Rajmahal Hills, outcome  [APPSC]

accepted.s: Which one of the following was an important cause of the Santhal Hul?
o: Oppression by zamindars, moneylenders and police
The abolition of the Khuntkatti system by the Santhals themselves
The transfer of Upper Assam to Purandar Singh
The introduction of bonded labour in Mewar
accepted.x: The Santhals faced oppression by zamindars, moneylenders, commonly called dikus, and the police. The Khuntkatti issue belonged principally to the Munda movement.
accepted.tq: Match the cause with the revolt instead of the similarly worded causes of other movements.
accepted.sec: Santhal Hul - Paharias, Rajmahal Hills, outcome  [APPSC]

accepted.s: After the Santhal Hul, which one of the following developments took place?
o: Santhal Parganas became a separate district with special laws protecting tribal land.
Upper Assam was restored to the Santhal leaders.
The Chotanagpur Tenancy Act was enacted in 1876.
Kolhan was placed under the Munda-Manki system immediately after the Ulgulan.
accepted.x: After the Hul, Santhal Parganas was created as a separate district and special laws were introduced to protect tribal land. The Chotanagpur Tenancy Act came later, in 1908.
accepted.tq: Find the correct post-revolt administrative consequence among closely related outcomes.
accepted.sec: Santhal Hul - Paharias, Rajmahal Hills, outcome  [APPSC]

accepted.s:
Consider the following statements:
1. The Santhal Parganas Tenancy Act is dated to 1876 in the cited chronology.
2. The current Santhal Parganas Tenancy Act is from 1949.
3. Santhal Parganas was created before the Santhal Hul.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
accepted.x: The 1876 date is associated with the Santhal Parganas Tenancy Act and the current Act is from 1949. Santhal Parganas was created after the Hul, so statement 3 is false.
accepted.tq: Spot the reversed before–after relationship in the third statement.
accepted.sec: Santhal Hul - Paharias, Rajmahal Hills, outcome  [APPSC]

accepted.s: Birsa Munda was born in:
accepted.x: Birsa Munda was born in 1875. He led the Ulgulan in 1899–1900.
accepted.tq: Separate the leader’s birth year from the years of his movement and its legal consequence.
accepted.sec: Birsa Munda - title, region, reform, Ulgulan, death  [APPSC]

accepted.s: Birsa Munda’s religious movement, which blended Munda tradition with Hinduism and Christianity, was known as:
accepted.x: Birsa Munda founded the monotheist Birsait faith, which blended elements of Munda tradition, Hinduism and Christianity.
accepted.tq: Use the exact name of the reform movement to distinguish it from later Bhil and Oraon movements.
accepted.sec: Birsa Munda - title, region, reform, Ulgulan, death  [APPSC]

accepted.s: Which one of the following was NOT part of Birsa Munda’s social and religious reform programme?
o: Opposition to animal sacrifice and spirit worship
Promotion of the Khuntkatti joint landholding system
accepted.x: Birsa’s programme opposed liquor, witchcraft, animal sacrifice and spirit worship and promoted a monotheist faith. Khuntkatti was a landholding system whose destruction helped cause the revolt; it was not a religious reform practice.
accepted.tq: Find the option that changes a land-rights issue into a reform practice.
accepted.sec: Birsa Munda - title, region, reform, Ulgulan, death  [APPSC]

accepted.s: The immediate agrarian grievance behind Birsa Munda’s revolt was the destruction of the:
accepted.x: The revolt was caused in part by the destruction of the Khuntkatti joint landholding system by zamindars, thikadars and missionaries.
accepted.tq: Identify the precise institution affected instead of choosing a general tribal-administration term.
accepted.sec: Birsa Munda - title, region, reform, Ulgulan, death  [APPSC]

accepted.s:
Consider the following statements about the Ulgulan:
1. It took place during 1899–1900.
2. Its objective included Abua Raj, or self-rule.
3. About 6,000 Mundas participated in it.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
accepted.x: The Ulgulan occurred in 1899–1900, aimed at Abua Raj and involved about 6,000 Mundas.
accepted.tq: Combine date, objective and participation figures in a single movement profile.
accepted.sec: Birsa Munda - title, region, reform, Ulgulan, death  [APPSC]

accepted.s: Which one of the following correctly describes the final phase of Birsa Munda’s life?
o: He was captured in February 1900 and died in Ranchi jail in June 1900.
He was captured in June 1900 and died in Bhognadih jail in February 1901.
He surrendered in 1899 and died in Khurda jail in 1908.
He was executed in 1905 after the enactment of the Chotanagpur Tenancy Act.
accepted.x: Birsa Munda was captured in February 1900 and died in Ranchi jail in June 1900.
accepted.tq: Use the sequence of capture, imprisonment and death to reject swapped dates and places.
accepted.sec: Birsa Munda - title, region, reform, Ulgulan, death  [APPSC]

accepted.s: The Chotanagpur Tenancy Act, 1908, associated with the consequences of the Ulgulan, is significant because it:
o: introduced the Eki movement in Mewar
created the Santhal Parganas as a separate district
handed Upper Assam to Purandar Singh
barred transfer of tribal land to non-tribals and recognised Khuntkatti rights
accepted.x: The Chotanagpur Tenancy Act, 1908, barred transfer of tribal land to non-tribals and recognised Khuntkatti rights.
accepted.tq: Infer the legal purpose from the land-rights grievance behind the movement.
accepted.sec: Birsa Munda - title, region, reform, Ulgulan, death  [APPSC]

accepted.s: Janjatiya Gaurav Divas is observed on 15 November in connection with the birth anniversary of:
accepted.x: 15 November, the birth anniversary of Birsa Munda, is observed as Janjatiya Gaurav Divas.
accepted.tq: Link the commemorative date with the correct tribal leader.
accepted.sec: Birsa Munda - title, region, reform, Ulgulan, death  [APPSC]

accepted.s: The Paika Rebellion of 1817 took place in:
accepted.x: The Paika Rebellion of 1817 took place in Khurda in present-day Odisha.
accepted.tq: Use the revolt–region association to distinguish Paika, Santhal, Bhil and Eki movements.
accepted.sec: Paika Rebellion and Ramosi uprisings  [APPSC]

accepted.s:
Which of the following was a major grievance of the Paikas in 1817?
1. Loss of rent-free lands after the British conquest of 1803
2. Salt policy and revenue burdens
3. Destruction of the Khuntkatti system
Select the correct answer using the code given below.
accepted.x: The Paikas lost rent-free lands after the 1803 conquest and also resented salt policy and revenue burdens. Destruction of Khuntkatti was a Munda grievance.
accepted.tq: Separate the Paika-specific economic grievances from the Munda landholding issue.
accepted.sec: Paika Rebellion and Ramosi uprisings  [APPSC]

accepted.s: The Paikas were traditionally:
o: moneylenders operating in the Rajmahal Hills
accepted.x: The Paikas were a traditional militia in the Khurda region whose rent-free lands were lost after the British conquest.
accepted.tq: Identify the occupational character of the group before testing the revolt’s causes.
accepted.sec: Paika Rebellion and Ramosi uprisings  [APPSC]

accepted.s: The Ramosis of Maharashtra rose against British rule mainly after the:
o: enactment of the Chotanagpur Tenancy Act
accepted.x: The Ramosis rose against British rule after the fall of the Peshwa.
accepted.tq: Link the revolt to its immediate political background rather than to a later legal measure.
accepted.sec: Paika Rebellion and Ramosi uprisings  [APPSC]

accepted.s:
Arrange the following tribal movements in chronological order of their beginning:
A. Santhal Hul
B. Ahom rebellion
C. Kol rising
D. Munda Ulgulan
accepted.x: The Ahom rebellion began in 1828, followed by the Kol rising in 1831–32, the Santhal Hul in 1855–56 and the Munda Ulgulan in 1899–1900.
accepted.tq: Fix the earliest and latest events first, then place the middle movements by year.
accepted.sec: Revolt → year matching and chronology  [other exams]

accepted.s: Which one of the following pairs is NOT correctly matched?
accepted.x: The Ahom rebellion occurred in 1828, not 1855–56. The other pairs correspond to the stated periods of the respective movements.
accepted.tq: Look for the single year-range mismatch in a revolt chronology table.
accepted.sec: Revolt → year matching and chronology  [other exams]

accepted.s: The Khasi rising of 1829–33 was led by:
accepted.x: The Khasi rising of 1829–33 was associated with Tirot Sing. Gomadhar Konwar led the Ahom rebellion.
accepted.tq: Distinguish the leaders of the Khasi and Ahom risings through direct pairing.
accepted.sec: Revolt → year matching and chronology  [other exams]

accepted.s: The Ahom rebellion resulted in the Company handing over Upper Assam to:
accepted.x: The Ahom rebellion forced the East India Company to hand Upper Assam to Purandar Singh.
accepted.tq: Match the political outcome with the correct regional rebellion.
accepted.sec: Revolt → year matching and chronology  [other exams]

accepted.s: Which one of the following statements regarding the Khasi rising is correct?
o: It began in 1899 as part of the Munda Ulgulan.
The standard chronology places it in 1829–33 under Tirot Sing.
It occurred in 1817 as a militia revolt in Khurda.
It was led by Purandar Singh against the Santhal settlement policy.
accepted.x: The standard chronology places the Khasi rising in 1829–33 under Tirot Sing. The other options confuse it with the Munda, Ahom and Paika movements.
accepted.tq: Resolve the chronology discrepancy by using the standard date and leader together.
accepted.sec: Revolt → year matching and chronology  [other exams]

accepted.s: Cleveland, the Collector of Bhagalpur in the 1780s, adopted a conciliatory plan for the Paharias by working through:
accepted.x: Cleveland’s conciliatory plan for the Paharias in the 1780s used hill chiefs. The Munda-Manki arrangement belonged to Wilkinson’s Rule in Kolhan.
accepted.tq: Ask who would perform the administrative role and distinguish the two colonial arrangements.
accepted.sec: Colonial tribal administration  [other exams]

accepted.s: Wilkinson’s Rule of 1837 is associated with the administration of Kolhan through:
accepted.x: Under Wilkinson’s Rule, introduced in 1837, Kolhan was governed through Munda-Manki chiefs after the Kol rising.
accepted.tq: Use the administrative authority–local institution pairing to avoid confusing Wilkinson’s Rule with Cleveland’s plan.
accepted.sec: Colonial tribal administration  [other exams]

accepted.s:
Which of the following constituted common causes of tribal revolts in colonial India?
1. Forest laws that made forests state property
2. Restrictions on podu or shifting cultivation
3. New land revenue demands
4. Land alienation caused by dikus
Select the correct answer using the code given below.
accepted.x: Forest laws, restrictions on podu cultivation, new revenue demands and land alienation caused by moneylenders, zamindars and traders were all important causes of tribal revolts.
accepted.tq: Treat the broad causal list as cumulative and check each economic and forest-related factor.
accepted.sec: Causes of tribal revolts  [other exams]

accepted.s: The Indian Forest Act of 1878 contributed to tribal discontent by treating forests as:
o: property of the Santhal Parganas district council
accepted.x: The Indian Forest Act of 1878 strengthened state control by making forests state property, adversely affecting tribal customary rights.
accepted.tq: Test the legal change in ownership rather than a general statement about forest administration.
accepted.sec: Causes of tribal revolts  [other exams]

accepted.s: In the context of tribal revolts, the term ‘dikus’ referred principally to:
accepted.x: Dikus were outsiders such as moneylenders, zamindars and traders whose activities contributed to tribal land alienation.
accepted.tq: Discriminate between a colonial social category and indigenous administrative institutions.
accepted.sec: Causes of tribal revolts  [other exams]

accepted.s: The common factor behind many tribal revolts, as identified in the broader interpretation of their causes, was the:
o: transfer of Upper Assam to Purandar Singh
complete disruption of the old agrarian order
accepted.x: A common underlying factor was the complete disruption of the old agrarian order through colonial revenue, forest and land policies.
accepted.tq: Move from individual causes to the wider structural explanation.
accepted.sec: Causes of tribal revolts  [other exams]

accepted.s: Govind Giri, also known as Guru, led the Bhils primarily against:
accepted.x: Govind Giri led the Bhils against bonded labour. His movement was associated with Rajasthan and Gujarat.
accepted.tq: Match the reform leader with the specific social grievance of the Bhils.
accepted.sec: Bhil reform movements in Rajasthan and Gujarat  [other exams]

accepted.s: The Mangarh massacre of 1913 is popularly known as the:
accepted.x: The Mangarh massacre of 1913 is called the “Adivasi Jallianwala.” Mangarh Dham was later recognised as a National Monument.
accepted.tq: Use the popular epithet to identify the correct tribal event.
accepted.sec: Bhil reform movements in Rajasthan and Gujarat  [other exams]

accepted.s: Mangarh Dham was declared a National Monument in:
accepted.x: Mangarh Dham, associated with the 1913 massacre, became a National Monument in 2022.
accepted.tq: Separate the date of the massacre from the much later date of official recognition.
accepted.sec: Bhil reform movements in Rajasthan and Gujarat  [other exams]

accepted.s: The Eki movement of 1921–22 in Mewar was led by:
accepted.x: Motilal Tejawat led the Eki movement in Mewar during 1921–22. Govind Giri was associated with the Bhil movement against bonded labour.
accepted.tq: Distinguish the two Bhil leaders by movement, region and period.
accepted.sec: Bhil reform movements in Rajasthan and Gujarat  [other exams]
